I've been working this land for 40 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The soil is decent, the well is reliable, and I follow the same rhythm my father taught me, adjusted over decades of my own experience.

**My thinking, crop by crop:**

My main system is wheat-maize on about 14 mu — that rotation is the backbone of what I do. The two crops share the same fields across the year. I keep 5.1 mu in cotton on a separate block. My family used to help more with cotton, but two of my sons work in the city now. At 64, I can't do endless spraying trips, so I keep BT hybrid cotton — less insect pressure, fewer applications.

For **wheat**, I'll plant improved variety seed, same Jimai series I've used for years. I know it performs here. Three irrigations: pre-winter to establish roots, then jointing, then heading. I'll apply compound fertilizer as base and urea as topdressing at jointing. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide early, one foliar fungicide near heading. Rotary tillage after maize harvest to turn the stalks in.

For **maize**, I'll go hybrid — Zhengdan 958 or similar, everyone around here uses it and it yields reliably. I plant right after wheat harvest in late June, sometimes no-till or light rotary depending on soil condition. Two irrigations. Corn doesn't need as much hand-holding as cotton.

For **cotton**, I'll plough in spring, plant in late April. Four irrigations throughout the long growing season — this crop is thirsty. Four pesticide applications even with BT seed; bollworm pressure still comes in late season. Labor is the constraint, so I plan my application windows carefully to avoid the hottest weeks.

My expected yields are realistic, not optimistic. I've seen bad years.
